name: Nam Giao Esplanade
kicker: Three terraces for heaven, earth, and man
summary: The open-air altar where Nguyễn kings offered sacrifice to heaven and earth: three stacked terraces, round on top and square below, in a pine grove south of the citadel. Walk the pine avenue under the flags to the circular upper terrace. Pair it with An Dinh, the other stop outside the walls.
getThere: South of the citadel (Trường An ward on the ticket record; Thuận Hóa ward on the monument list).
heroCaption: The pine walk and flags toward the Nam Giao terraces

notice.title: No ceremony date this year
notice.body: The Nam Giao rite was held every spring from 1807 until Thành Thái, then every three years from 1907. No date is published for this year, so do not plan the day around it.

body: The altar was first set at An Ninh village in 1803 and moved south of the citadel in 1806.

Three tiers stack heaven, earth, and man. The top is a circle with a green rail. The middle is a square with a yellow rail. The bottom is a square with a red rail. Doors and steps open on all four sides. Pines, once planted by the court, still frame the walk.
An adult ticket is 50,000 VND, and children under 13 enter free.

figures.caption: The circular top terrace and its railing
figures.alt: The round upper terrace of Nam Giao among pines

gettingThere: The esplanade is south of the citadel. Ask for Nam Giao, in Trường An or Thuận Hóa ward; the two official lists use different ward names.
hours: 16 Mar–15 Oct: 06:30–18:00, tickets until 17:30. 16 Oct–15 Mar: 07:00–17:30, tickets until 17:00 (conservation centre notice, 12 Mar 2024). Confirm the board on arrival.
closed: No weekly closing day on the centre’s notice.
admissionNote: Adult 50,000 VND. A child from 7 to 12 is free. Under 7 is free. Hue residents and the other groups named in Resolution 55 pay half. This is not the Imperial City ticket.
